findings.headline: Stress rise on lap 33 despite flat pace – visor visibility and tyre wear likely culprits
findings.detail: The driver’s stress spiked to 31.4 on lap 33 (radio call without context) while on a four‑lap‑old Intermediate tyre in wet conditions; pace delta was flat (+0.000) but the model suggests the tyre was already losing grip (modelled deg -0.199 s/lap). This indicates the driver felt uneasy despite stable lap times, likely due to reduced visibility and tyre wear, so a clearer visor and earlier tyre change could reduce stress.

findings.headline: Medium tyres delivered instant pace gain after wet‑dry crossover
findings.detail: During the wet‑to‑dry crossover at lap 40 the driver switched back to Medium tyres (lap 40) on a dry track (24.6 °C) and immediately posted a -0.098 s pace improvement on lap 41, showing the Medium’s superior dry performance; however, stress data is missing, so the driver’s confidence cannot be confirmed. Recommend keeping Mediums for post‑crossover phases when track temps rise above 24 °C.

findings.headline: Late switch to Intermediates caused >11 s loss on lap 19
findings.detail: The massive +11.779 s pace delta on lap 19 coincided with the first wet sensor activation; the driver stayed on a Medium tyre (age 19) which the model suggests was ill‑suited (+0.173 s/lap degradation). Switching to Intermediates at lap 27 reduced the pace delta to 0.000, confirming the tyre choice was the main limiter. Advise earlier wet‑tyre switch when rain sensor first triggers.
evidence: pace delta +0.000 on lap 27 after switch to INTERMEDIATE

findings.headline: Low post‑race stress confirms final Medium stint was well‑chosen
findings.detail: Stress reading of 13.2 on lap 52 (post‑race) is not in‑race, but the driver described the strategy as “right decisions” after a dry finish (track 25.3 °C). This suggests the driver felt comfortable with the final Medium stint, which modelled degradation was negligible (-0.009 s/lap). No action needed, but reinforces that the final tyre choice was appropriate.

findings.headline: Driver held pace under blue flags on wet Mediums
findings.detail: Blue flags appeared from lap 21 to 27 while the driver was on a wet Medium tyre; pace delta stayed near zero (+0.000 to +0.000) indicating the driver managed traffic without losing time, but stress data is absent. With limited data (no stress readings), confidence is moderate; still, maintaining focus under blue‑flag conditions on sub‑optimal tyres is a positive sign.
evidence: compound MEDIUM age 21‑25 on those laps

findings.headline: Minor slowdown on lap 48 hints at late‑stage Medium tyre wear
findings.detail: A small pace increase of +0.268 s on lap 48 occurred on a dry Medium tyre (age 9) after a long stint; the model suggests slight degradation (+0.173 s/lap) may be contributing, but with only one data point and no stress reading, the pattern is weak. Monitor tyre wear in the final phase of future races.
